title: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
biology: Ecologists compare parasite burdens among fish from two independent lakes.
design: Each fish is sampled once; counts are strongly skewed and tied.
data_characteristics: Ordinal or continuous response, including ranked counts
Uses relative ordering rather than raw distances
other_examples: Ordinal disease scores in two treatments
question: Do parasite-burden distributions differ between the two lakes?
null: The two groups have the same response distribution.
options: exact = FALSE handles these tied counts
Location-shift interpretation needs similarly shaped distributions
assumptions: Different shapes/spreads can affect the result
parametric: Negative-binomial regression models the count response directly
Welch t tests a mean difference when that is the target
nonparametric: Use signed-rank or sign for paired observations

plot_args.note: Map lake and burden to axes

practice: If your target is the ratio of mean parasite counts, would a rank-sum result answer that directly?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1106)
d <- data.frame(lake = rep(c("Clear", "Reedy"), each = 32),
                parasites = c(rnbinom(32, mu = 5, size = 1.5),
                              rnbinom(32, mu = 10, size = 1.5)))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
p <- ggplot(d, aes(lake, parasites, color = lake)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = 0, size = 2.7, alpha = .75) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 5, color = "black") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#246A73", "#B7663E")) +
  labs(x = "Lake", y = "Parasites per fish", caption = "Black diamonds: group medians") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) + theme(legend.position = "none")
print(p)
code_analysis:
fit <- wilcox.test(parasites ~ lake, data = d,
                   exact = FALSE, correct = TRUE)
generating_model: 32 independent fish per lake have negative-binomial parasite counts. Clear has mean 5 and Reedy mean 10, both with size parameter 1.5; variances are mean + mean squared / 1.5.
generating_truth: The lake distributions differ, including their mean and spread. The same-distribution null is false; there is not a simple equal-shape location shift.
teaching_point: A rank-sum result can reflect distributional differences; the mean-count question also has a direct count-model route.
